# SOP: operating and debugging casts

## Safe-testing rules

1. **Ask before casting to a TV.** The Chromecast and Office TV are family
   TVs; a cast takes over whatever the kids are watching. Build and test on the
   local TV desktop (`raytube-tv up` without casting) until the user says go.
2. **Never `pkill -f` / `pgrep -f` with a pattern that appears in your own
   command line.** It kills the calling shell (exit 144). Use saved PIDs,
   `pkill -x <name>`, or a pattern like `'board[.]py'`.
3. **Minimise screenshots.** Each `grim` adds to the Hyprland screen-share
   leak. Capture one output (`grim -o eDP-1` or `grim -o TV`); with the TV
   output present a plain `grim` captures both monitors side by side. Never use
   a full-screen capture as a "bar" crop: it can include other private windows.
4. **Build at low priority during a cast:** `GOMAXPROCS=2 nice -n 19 go build -p 2`,
   `nice -n 19 cargo build -j 2`.
5. Don't benchmark during a live cast: it starves capture and trips the guard.

## Everyday use

```bash
raytube-cast list                       # receivers: name, ip, paired, airplay|cast
raytube-cast mode mirror|desktop        # what gets cast
raytube-cast start <chromecast-ip> "Chromecast HD"
raytube-cast toggle <apple-tv-ip> "Office TV"   # stop if casting there, else start (Display menu row)
raytube-cast status                     # on<TAB>ip<TAB>name<TAB>mode | off
raytube-cast stop                       # also takes the TV desktop down
raytube-cast release                    # end the cast, keep the TV desktop (native YouTube)
raytube-cast tv                         # TV mode O: toggle the TV desktop to the last receiver
raytube-cast size <apple-tv-ip> 1080p   # picture size for an Apple TV: 720p|1080p|1440p (restarts the cast)
raytube-cast av-delay <apple-tv-ip> 50  # sound delay in ms for an Apple TV (applied live)
raytube-cast av-delay-step -50          # nudge the current TV's sound earlier/later (Display menu − / +)
raytube-cast resync                     # restart the session: back in sync (Display menu Re-sync TV, TV mode A)
raytube-tv json                         # TV desktop state
raytube-tv browser "<url>"              # TV browser in the Watch scene
raytube-tv board                        # family board
raytube-tv layout next | swap | video-full
raytube-tv native | pull                # Chromecast's own YouTube app and back (untested on device, T-2)
```

**Watchdog.** `raytube-cast` does not start `cast-watch.sh`; start it once per login with
`systemd-run --user --unit=raytube-watch $PWD/cast-watch.sh` (check with
`systemctl --user is-active raytube-watch`). Without it there is no xrun escalation and no
automatic re-sync.

**Fans loud or CPU hot?** The guard's quiet curve and turbo-off (`TURBO=0`) only apply while
a cast runs. Look at `~/.local/state/raytube/thermal.log`, then at other load (Firefox video,
MCP servers, builds).

**Test without a TV (AirPlay):** `project-references/doubletake/bin/doubletake-test-receiver -listen
127.0.0.1:7000 &` then `TARGET=127.0.0.1 timeout -s INT 15 ./cast-tv.sh`; the receiver's final stats
line counts video and audio frames received.

**Sound and picture out of sync?** First check the picture size: an Apple TV held a
2560x1440 picture ~0.9 s behind the sound, while 720p and 1080p stay in sync. Only then use
the Sound sync − / + (Office TV: 50 ms). Test with `raytube-tv browser file://$PWD/av-sync-test.html`
(flash + beep every 4 s).

**Choppy sound?** Look for PipeWire xruns, not doubletake errors (its drops only log with
`-debug`): `pw-top -b -n 2`, ERR column for `Firefox` and `gst-launch-1.0`. Casts run a
1024-sample cycle; `cast-watch.sh` raises it to 2048 if glitches return and logs each one
with context in `~/.local/state/raytube/cast-watch.log`.

**Timing during a live AirPlay cast:** restart the unit with `cast-tv.sh -debug` (see
`raytube-cast` start for the env) and run `sync-watch.sh` (unit `raytube-syncwatch`) for a
per-minute summary of fps, source age and slack in `~/.local/state/raytube/sync-watch.log`.

## Self-test without watching the TV (Chromecast)

`./cc-selftest.sh 30` casts for 30 s and prints a PASS/FAIL verdict from the
receiver's own RTCP: checkpoints ≈ fps received complete, keyframe requests =
decoder trouble. During a normal cast, read the same lines:

```bash
sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' ~/.local/state/omacast/omacastd.log | grep -E "receiver( audio)?:" | tail
```

For AirPlay, `-debug` logs show `source age` / `slack` per 5 s; slack must stay
positive (frames arriving before their display time).

## Debugging checklist

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Nothing on the TV | `systemctl --user status raytube-cast`, `journalctl --user -u raytube-cast` |
| `Invalid or missing codec on first OFFER` | SSRC range patch present? (see cast-pipeline) |
| `connecting to [fe80::…]` | discovery IPv4 patch present? |
| Low fps, Hyprland CPU high | `perf` on Hyprland: `outputCopyFBState` → screen-share leak, re-login |
| Picture freezes, audio continues | capture stalled: `WF` errors in the log; display mode change → the launcher restarts |
| Blocky / "Unrepairable underflow" | wf-recorder must get `-B <fps>` |
| Growing delay | frames late: raise `LATENCY_MS`, keep steady frames (`-D`) |
| Audio crackle | PipeWire xruns: `pw-top` ERR column; pulsesrc chunks ≥20 ms; cycle 1024 (`pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.force-quantum`) |
| Audio silent after CPU spike | audio stuck late → doubletake restarts only the audio capture (a third stall in a minute restarts everything); then `raytube-cast resync` |
| Sound and picture drift apart after glitches | `raytube-cast resync` (Display menu Re-sync TV, TV mode A); the Apple TV never catches up by itself |
| Picture held well behind sound (Apple TV) | picture size too big: `raytube-cast size <ip>` should be 720p or 1080p |
| CPU hot | `~/.local/state/raytube/thermal.log`; check other load (Firefox software decode) |

## Measuring latency

Open `latency-test.html` full screen (F11), calibrate on the laptop, then time
flashes on the TV. The result subtracts reaction time. Discard trials where the
TV phase started before the cast was up.

## Test plan (TV desktop), one step at a time

1. Mirror to the Chromecast (Screen chip). 2. Switch to TV desktop mid-cast.
3. ⌘⌃↑ a window to the TV, ⌘⌃↓ back. 4. Board button. 5. `raytube-tv
browser <youtube url>`. 6. TV mode L through the cycle, then M. 7. TV mode N / P. 8. TV mode R rotation.
9. TV mode Y native YouTube and back. 10. `raytube-tv pull`. 11. TV mode O stop.
12. Office TV. Steps 1–3 passed on the Chromecast (2026-09-26); on the Office TV the desktop,
send/back, board, TV browser, split and PiP passed. Status per step lives in TASKS.md (T-1, T-2,
T-4). Rotation seconds are shortened to 15 for testing; restore from
`~/.config/raytube/tv.json.before-test` (T-3).
